brief: Goldman trader Matthew Kaplan reports hedge funds had their worst cross-strategy day since the 2011 US downgrade: Fundamental Long/Short, Systematic and Multi-Strat funds were each down more than 1% simultaneously for the first time since Covid, and the HF VIP vs. most-shorted pair (GSTHVIPP) fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011 and now down 10.4% month-to-date, after hedge fund short leverage had already reached a 5-year high. The trigger was an AI-capex-driven equity selloff (S&P -1.5%, Nasdaq 100 down over 3% on Meta, Lam Research and Tesla), which reflexively drove Treasuries' largest 10Y yield drop since August 2025 (about 15bps), because AI weakness eases prospective bond issuance and pulls CTA model triggers toward further buying. AI credit risk diverged, with Meta's CDS spiking on higher spending plans and Tesla's on lower ones, and French 10Y yields topped US Treasuries for the first time since 2013. Despite the index fall, 335 S&P names rose and Goldman's ex-AI index outperformed by 6% MTD; the piece frames this breadth-versus-index split as a liquidation rather than a relief rally, noting desks saw no dip-buying.
